title: Respond to an outcome without making it your worth

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: An outcome can require accountability without determining worth. Equal dignity leaves ordinary care available and also leaves real obligations intact; self-respect is not an exemption from repair.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fictional Ari promised a draft by 15:00, forgot, and sends it 16:00. Jo had to delay their own review 30 minutes; no financial loss is supplied. Jo accepts a short acknowledgment and does not request a gift. Ari has an ordinary evening meal and rest planned. A next task is not due until tomorrow.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Separate event, known impact and identity story. Draft a proportionate response and preserve ordinary care without claiming the mistake did not matter.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A person says “my worth is unconditional, so I need not return the borrowed tool.” What should be corrected?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Own the missed time and 30-minute impact, acknowledge it and use a suitable future reminder. Later fiction: acknowledgment is received; forgiveness is not reported. Meal and rest remain legitimate. Partial: affirm dignity but omit the missed promise. Incorrect: withhold food or use worth language to deny the effect.
criteria: Event and identity claims are separated
Basic care is not earned through success

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: Worth is not conditional on the tool, but the actual borrowing obligation remains. Return or appropriately renegotiate it; accountability does not require self-condemnation.
criteria: Event and identity claims are separated
